rows.label: Scenario 1: Government costs would replace HKI's costs
Scenario 1: Government costs would replace HKI's costs (Not specified)
rows.explainer: Our understanding is that VAS in the regions Helen Keller would support has not received external funding for several years. The government provides support for VAS in Madagascar through the health system (we account for the impact of government support on baseline coverage in our "double treatment" adjustment above), which may sometimes be delivered through community outreach programs. However, given the fairly longstanding status quo of lack of external funding, we think it's very unlikely that the government would increase its support for VAS in Helen Keller's absence to a level that is similar to what Helen Keller typically provides.

rows.label: Percentage of total costs covered by Nutrition International (vitamin A capsule procurement) (Madagascar)
Nutrition International (vitamin A capsule procurement) (Not specified)
Percentage of total program costs covered by other philanthropic actors (Madagascar)
rows.explainer: We use the "overall" cost estimates from our cost per supplement analysis here because we do not have direct cost information for Madagascar. Because our "overall" cost estimates are averages across countries, they assume that about 13% of program costs, on average, will be covered by philanthropic actors other than Helen Keller. However, in reality, we think it's unlikely that other philanthropic actors will contribute to VAS in Madagascar, so we have instead added this 13% to the proportion of costs covered by Helen Keller and assumed that costs covered by other philanthropic actors will be 0%.
